localBiteReport: Note: The most recent available reports are from late September to early October 2026 — roughly 1 to 2.5 weeks old — so conditions may have shifted somewhat since then. That said, the fall bite on Choctawhatchee Bay is shaping up well. Redfish are the standout inshore species right now, with guides reporting active action around bayou docks, grass flats, and drop-offs; one Santa Rosa Beach guide noted slot reds biting well around dock structure. Speckled trout are still in the mix, showing up around dock lights at night and on deeper flat edges, though sheepshead are expected to improve further as fall progresses. Flounder gigging was noted as picking up in early September and typically stays productive through October as fish stage near passes. Water temperature at this location is 81°F.
